summary: Phase 1 (JWT auth + user management) tested end-to-end. 19/19 pytest tests passed. Covered: admin login success/failure, cookie set + Bearer token, /auth/me hides password_hash, unauthenticated 401s, /users admin-only (403 for depo/muhasebe), duplicate username 409, PATCH updates including password (verified by re-login), self-delete 400, delete user 200, role matrix (muhasebe can access dashboard/materials/products/orders/customers/summary but not /users), all legacy endpoints (materials CRUD, products, configurator templates/estimate/seed, orders POST/PATCH, transactions, customers credit-sales/payments/summary/history) work with Bearer token, and admin seed idempotency (single admin user after multiple restarts).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py auth_gate middleware runs AFTER CORSMiddleware add order; because Starlette wraps middleware LIFO, the auth_gate runs innermost — OK for /api routes but ensure OPTIONS bypass is correct (it is).
auth.py seed_admin uses ADMIN_USERNAME/ADMIN_PASSWORD with defaults 'admin'/'admin'. Fine because .env sets strong password, but consider raising if env missing in production.
auth.py has an unused/broken require_roles stub that duplicates server.py logic — dead code, remove to avoid confusion.
Login sets cookie with samesite=none secure=true which requires HTTPS. Documented in task; Bearer path works.

server.py: PATCH /materials/{id} allows unauthenticated updates via middleware but middleware protects — verified. Same file has no role restrictions on writes (any authenticated user can create/update materials/orders/etc). Consider tightening with warehouse/accounting/shipping deps that are defined but unused.
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral TEST_-prefixed users created and deleted per test. TEST customer/material/order/transaction records left in DB (non-destructive, prefixed 'TEST').
context_for_next_testing_agent: All auth flows validated via Bearer token against public URL. Use test file /app/backend/tests/test_auth_and_endpoints.py as regression. The role-based dependencies (warehouse, accounting, shipping) are defined in server.py but not applied to any endpoints — currently every authenticated user has full CRUD on materials/orders/etc except /api/users which is admin_only. If Phase 2 introduces role-scoped writes, add tests for those.
rca of the issue: N/A — no unresolved issues. One initial test failure (unknown product type 'masa') was a test-side issue; fixed by pulling actual template key from /api/configurator/templates.
